All children at our schools learn about children's rights through the Rights, Respecting School programme, which is underpinned by the UNCRC (United Nations Convention of the Rights of the Child). The school has been awarded Rights Respecting School (RRS) status and this is reflected in the school ethos and approach to behaviour. 'The Knights' Way’ (school values), along with our RRS work provides a fundamental platform for learning about ‘British Values’. Sports Premium
The PE and sport premium is designed to help primary schools improve the quality of the PE and sport activities they offer their pupils. Schools receive PE and sport premium funding based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6. Schools must spend the funding to improve the quality of the PE and sport activities they offer their pupils, but they are free to choose the best way of using the money.
We have decided to focus on training and development to meet the requirements of the new National Curriculum alongside offering our pupils the opportunity to experience sports and activities that they may not have access to at present. We aim to encourage pupils to participate in physical activity both in school and outside of school. We are also keen to build their confidence and self-esteem through controlled risk taking and team building activities.
Impact of the Sports Premium Funding:
The funding has allowed us to offer more children the opportunity to participate in after school clubs by subsidising the cost. As a result more children have attended these clubs. Our equipment has been updated to offer teachers and coaches the opportunities to fully develop the skills necessary to help pupils to excel in a broad range of physical activities. EYFS has benefitted by being able to develop their balance and core muscles on the climbing wall and use of tricycles. CPD has enabled the teachers to maximise the potential in pupils and also develop their skills. We have been able to attend all of the tournaments in our cluster due to the funding which enables us to provide transport.
How will we monitor the impact of the Sports Premium Funding:
The schools will be monitoring both the physical development & engagement levels of pupils through teacher observation and an assessment system and quality assurance measures.
The school will continue to offer a variety of after-school sports clubs over the next academic year and will be closely monitoring the attendance to ensure maximum take up.
The schools will continue to maximise opportunities for both in school and out of school sporting competitions. The results of the competitions will be shared via the website & school newsletter

Mental Health and Wellbeing Policy 2026
Emotional Health and Wellbeing
Over the last couple of years, mental health and wellbeing has had to be and will continue to be a huge part of education, more so than it ever has been. We are, of course, educators and not psychologists however, we recognise the growing need for support for our pupils and how swamped external mental health support services are.
We currently offer mental health and wellbeing provision in varying forms and levels of intensity, with a view to ensuring these interventions have the desired impact on our pupils. All of our provision is structured and robust, none of it should be a long term solution and those pupils we have concerns about, are assessed to ensure they receive the correct support.
Please see below for our graduated approach to supporting mental health and wellbeing:
This support is not necessarily isolated to one intervention at a time in the order shown; we may feel a child would benefit from regular check-ins alongside weekly wellbeing support, or perhaps they need a ZoR intervention whilst we wait for a CAMHS referral to go through. Perhaps a THRIVE intervention alone is enough to address their area of need and we just need to check in regularly to ensure all is well. So this support can take on a variety of forms and is very much about the needs of the individual.
However, it is also important to recognise that as a school, the children’s emotional needs are at the forefront of what we do on a day to day basis, whether it be myself checking in with pupils, rewards and celebrations of achievement, our regular PSHE curriculum sessions or our numerous enrichment opportunities.
I am hoping this gives you some insight into what we deliver and the importance we place on this aspect of your child’s development.
If you have any questions, please contact Mrs White Deputy Head via the Infant Office on 01264 352151.

Together We Believe…in making life better for Young Carers
We have ten percent of children on roll recognised as Young Carers (YC) who currently attend Andover Young Carers (AYC) weekly or monthly. We work closely with AYC and local support services in adopting a recognised referral system to help identify and work with Young Carers and their families.
We believe all children should have the same life opportunities and the right to reach their full potential regardless of responsibilities at home. We know that supporting children holistically and offering help when needed improves outcomes for our children. At Knights Enham Schools we are passionate about making the lives of Young Carers better through a programme of promoting YC’s awareness with children, families and staff. We offer pastoral support, regular drop in sessions with AYC and promote a strong spiritual, moral, social and cultural awareness through our curriculum. Children accessing YC support share positive influences to fellow YC’s who may need reassurance and kindness.
